body.body:
## What

Move YAML reading and writing to `serde-saphyr` and link sibling releases that remove libyaml translations from the engine’s dependency graph. Remove the temporary advisory ignore and ban all seven replaced YAML crates from returning.

Add regression coverage for existing configuration values, actionable parse errors, and shadow-store documents read back and edited by onetaskgraph. Extend dependency checks to cover the bus, budget library and each linked onetaskgraph crate individually.

## Why

Every dispatch carried unmaintained translated C through the engine and its dependencies. This removes that code while preserving the meaning of existing configuration documents and keeping write-back documents readable and editable by the plan store.

## Additional info

Downstream Rust consumers using the `onetaskgraph_*` types exposed by onepipeline must align with the exact `0.7.1` release linked by this branch.

## What

Link onevcs 0.52.0 and onevcs-testing 0.19.4 so idle pool maintenance runs each repository’s declared command. Preserve per-slot disk measurements in the journal and show reclaimed GiB, contributing slots, and repositories in `results`, alongside unreadable declarations.

Add real maintenance journeys and a release-only workload budget covering 25 slots across 20 repositories. Bump the rustls lockfile entry to 0.23.46 for security fixes.

## Why

Repositories’ cleanup of roughly 926 GB of superseded build output must reach every host running the engine. Reporting reclaimed space makes that cleanup visible, while surfacing unreadable declarations exposes stopped maintenance before the pool fills the disk.

body.body:
## What

Consolidate macOS coverage into one sequential PR job and one pre-publication release job, preserving Linux/Windows coverage and protected check names. Semantic release-only PRs, base pushes and downstream smoke request no Mac runner; manual Mac diagnostics default off.

**Intel macOS artifacts are discontinued from the next release.** Apple Silicon retains archive, wheel and npm packaging with native install/smoke checks before publication.

## Why

The shared five-runner macOS pool spends several scarce slots on one change, leaving otherwise green work and dependent releases queued. Consolidating existing proofs and builds returns slots to other changes.

## Additional info

### Scheduling and release compatibility

Baseline: `bdd2b29578a0dcbb2236bb1f0516bc90e60f9692`. Finished head: `6fa78f1a95a5a0084ba535819e53fe4f5db84779`. It retains `c30c5dc70f648116f1b7487ab9f354a081427cc1`, merges main at `e28ee8eaefb1cc99a377d85ee11d48083f208fad` through `810345e0`, and subsequently merges main at `26a06e55` through `5dcbee94`.

The merged CI retains main’s Windows per-leg verdict and 220-minute job/180-minute cross-check limits. Both consolidated Mac proof jobs have the 180-minute cross-check limit and 240-minute job limits, leaving time for reruns and installs.

These counts describe **modelled workflow routes**, not observed runner executions. The contract interpreter expands actual matrices, evaluates Actions expressions, traverses the pinned reusable workflow and follows downstream triggers. Unsupported resolution fails explicitly.

| Workflow | Triggering events, before → after | Mac jobs/run before | Mac jobs/run after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ci.yml` | push, pull_request → push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch | 3: cross, install, install-documented | Ordinary PR: 1; semantic release-only PR and base push: 0; manual default: 0; opted-in diagnostic: 1, outside the lifecycle |
| `release.yml` | release → unchanged | 10: upload ×2, build-wheels ×2, build-npm ×2, verify-pypi ×2, verify-npm ×2; Apple Silicon and Intel, with Intel removed by this change | 1 Apple Silicon build/install job across publish-flag combinations |
| `published-smoke.yml` | workflow_run, workflow_dispatch → unchanged | 4: PyPI and npm on Apple Silicon and Intel, with Intel removed by this change | 0 |
| `engine-currency.yml` | push, pull_request, workflow_dispatch → unchanged | 0 | 0 |
| `notignored.yml` | pull_request → unchanged | 0 | 0 |
| `release-plz.yml` | push → unchanged | 0 | 0 |
| `release-sweep.yml` | pull_request → unchanged | 0 | 0 |
| `visual-docs.yml`, including pinned screencomp v0.4.8 reusable call | pull_request, push, schedule → unchanged | 0 | 0 |

| Release platform | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux x86_64 | Archive + checksum, wheel + SBOM, npm package | Unchanged |
| Linux aarch64 | Archive + checksum, wheel + SBOM, npm package | Unchanged |
| Apple Silicon macOS | Archive + checksum, wheel + SBOM, npm package | Retained; built, installed and run natively in one job; release attachment and publication run on Linux |
| Intel macOS | `x86_64-apple-darwin` archive + checksum, Intel wheel + SBOM, `onepipeline-cli-darwin-x64` | **Removed from the next release** |
| Windows x86_64 | Archive + checksum, wheel + SBOM, npm package | Unchanged |

The launcher package and crates.io crate remain. Darwin packaging retains bundled helper executables, README, license, changelog, flat archive layout and checksum names. One compiled payload feeds its archive, wheel and npm forms, with content hashes checked. Native Apple Silicon install/smoke checks precede publication; there is no Rosetta or Intel cross-compilation step. The npm launcher explicitly refuses Intel macOS and recommends building from source with `cargo install onepipeline --locked`; the packed-launcher test covers that refusal. `release-targets.toml` records the discontinued npm package as retired.

Recorded telemetry reports **1 Mac job/run** and **2 Mac-spending runs/change**, within both registered budgets. It covers twelve event classes, three diff classes, same-repository/fork ownership, publish combinations and lifecycles with and without a release PR. The uncached Nx workflow test records telemetry; SDK reporters read it and reject missing or stale records. Only the budget checker compares measurements with thresholds.

Each budget registration’s description records the approved exception: the brief requires both per-run and per-change ceilings, and both remain separate. One run can occupy several shared Mac slots even when the lifecycle count remains within its bound; the jobs/run description carries this `inner_measure_reason`. Neither registration has a separate rationale comment or a `budgets_track_product_owner_outcomes` marker because that rule is not configured here. Existing budget thresholds and lint rules are unchanged.

### Routing and required contexts

The shared semantic classifier authorizes Mac omission only for a same-repository `release-plz-` branch whose parsed diff changes versions/changelog alone. Author identity cannot authorize omission. Forks, forged or mixed release branches, registry dependency changes—including a dependency named `onepipeline`—and unreadable PR input require Mac coverage. Unknown event names fail closed with the event named in the reason; known non-PR automatic events do not request the CI Mac lane.

Linux carriers retain the protected Mac display names and the path-selected `cross (windows-latest)`, `install (ubuntu-latest)`, `install (windows-latest)` and `wheel` contexts. They use `always()` and explicit prerequisite/per-leg outcomes, reject failed, cancelled or missing required work, and label authorized omissions without claiming tests ran. Proof jobs have distinct names. This branch does not edit branch protection; release-compat remains its separately selected tier.

The previous conditional matrices could leave rendered contexts unreported when the crate was unaffected, `changes` failed or `gate` prevented installation. The carriers close those gaps. `install-documented (*)` remains unconditional. The existing non-matrix `deny`, `msrv`, `smoke` and `release-compat` jobs retain their path-sensitive skips under their existing names. Contract tests enumerate protected contexts across source, dependency and release-only PR shapes, affected/unaffected selection and failed/cancelled prerequisites.

The CI-only `github-workflows:test` failure at `1aaabfa3` came from Nx setting `FORCE_COLOR`: `console.log(boolean)` inserted ANSI colour escapes into the classifier’s GitHub output. Production now uses `process.stdout.write(String(...))`, and its subprocess test sets `FORCE_COLOR=1`. The failure was reproduced in a fresh clone with the gate environment; the repaired clone passed 41 tests and both budgets.

The finished tree uses **`gpt-6.1-sol`** as judged lint’s Codex primary, including its explanatory comments; fallbacks and other harness settings remain unchanged. Main now carries that configuration too, so it is no longer an outstanding difference against the merged base.

### Latest local evidence and draft status

On the final tree committed as `6fa78f1a`, the workflow project’s budgets, lint, format-check and syntax-check targets passed. Its test dependency passed **43/43** tests and regenerated telemetry; both budgets passed at **1 job/run** and **2 runs/change**. The final test change adds subprocess assertions for extra `path-carrier` arguments and unknown/missing CLI modes.

`just lint-llm-diff origin/main`, against `26a06e55`, passed without a harness override: **24 passed, 0 failed, 14 skipped, 1 not relevant**, history `20261016T081620Z-98ad4`. The retained Codex rollout records **`gpt-6.1-sol`**.

At the last recorded exact-head read of [PR #885](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/pull/885), the remote head was `6fa78f1a`. Changes, gate, llmlint, both documented-install jobs, engine currency, suppressions and visual-docs architecture selection were **pending**. PR title and visual-docs preflight had **passed**; the manual Mac diagnostic, release sweep and host budgets were **skipped**. This observation is not a completed required-check verdict.

No repository-wide gate was run locally and no Release was published. Darwin release execution remains evidence to obtain from a release run; Linux journeys do not claim to execute Darwin binaries. Release-only PRs, base pushes, release builds, downstream triggers and manual dispatch routing are contract-level evidence rather than observed executions.

### Retained earlier verification

These results describe the specified earlier trees; they are not newly rerun checks or a claim that all required checks on the final head are green.

- At `810345e0`, workflow tests passed **43/43**, both budgets passed, `cargo test --locked --test ci_workflows` passed **8/8**, and actionlint passed on the merged `ci.yml`. Judged lint against `e28ee8ea` passed: **30 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped, 3 not relevant**, history `20261016T060154Z-149b5`. That history identifies Codex but does not independently record the model; the configured primary was `gpt-6.1-sol`.
- At `0a095ac`, workflow tests passed **43/43**, telemetry was regenerated and both budgets passed. Judged lint against `d8d674f` passed: **31 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped, 2 not relevant**, history `20261015T133335Z-fa586`.
- At `ff69b82`, judged lint passed without a harness override: **30 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped, 3 not relevant**, history `20261015T131635Z-4a8f9`. That commit changed only the primary model and explanatory comments.
- The carrier repair’s focused `ci_workflows`, `nextest_runs` and `linux_wheel` checks passed **34 tests**. Actionlint, Biome lint/format and `cargo fmt --check` were clean. Judged lint passed against `af2f7eb`, history `20261014T031804Z-7b848`.
- At `2ce7e0b`, real npm launcher/packaging journeys passed **76/76**, and `package_bundle` passed. These exercise the real host-native Linux archive/wheel/npm build, pack, install and smoke commands used by the release workflow, with registry publication and forge transport doubled. Mutation journeys reject malformed wheel metadata/tags, unsafe or duplicate members, unsupported install schemes and missing executable bits.
- `publish-gate`, `platform-matrix`, `release-targets`, `release-outcome`, `release_targets` and `published_smoke` passed on an earlier trial merge with main. That trial was not retained because publication refused an unrelated line at `docs/windows-journey-audit.md:177`, introduced on main in #892.
- At `c30c5dc`, the npm launcher journey passed **76/76**, using isolated `target/npm-staged` builds and writing nothing to shared `target/<host-triple>`. Judged lint passed on the configured `gpt-6.1-sol` primary without an override: **31 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped, 2 not relevant**, history `20261015T150802Z-9baf9`.

### Historical draft-run observations and follow-ups

Statuses below describe the named commits and observation times, not the final head.

- At `fce1179`, [CI run 38505561149](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38505561149), read complete at 2026-10-15T13:17Z, **failed overall**. Its only Mac job, [Mac PR proofs](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38505561149/job/115662635891), and all three Mac carriers **passed**; the manual diagnostic was **skipped**. Gate, including the repaired workflow test, passed. Linux/Windows install proofs and protected carriers, documented installs, wheel proofs/carrier, llmlint, deny, msrv, pr-title and release-compat passed.
- That run’s Windows cross proof was **cancelled** at its then-unchanged 130-minute timeout after reaching test 1137/1292 with tests passing; its protected carrier correctly **failed**. Baseline runs [38663584742](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38663584742) and [38660020099](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38660020099) also encountered Windows timeouts. Live smoke failed when GitHub’s API rate limit refused cleanup reads, outside this change’s scope.
- Also at `fce1179`, [Release sweep 38505561130](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38505561130) was **completed/skipped** for the ordinary PR, and [Visual docs 38505561423](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38505561423) **passed**.
- At `ff69b82`, [CI run 38741360674](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38741360674) and Visual docs were **queued at publication**; release sweep, notignored and engine currency were in progress. These observations do not establish completed proof.
- At `0a095ac`, [CI run 38743772630](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38743772630) **failed gate** on `tests/build_config.rs`’s `dev_test_and_release_builds_carry_no_debuginfo`: it timed out at 360 seconds, then passed **3/3** reruns from the same archived build. The npm staged `maturin build --target <host>` journey built from cold in shared `target/`, holding its build lock for minutes (`onepipeline-npm:test` took 836 seconds). `c30c5dc` isolates those builds in `target/npm-staged`. At approximately 14:47Z, other completed checks had passed, Mac and Windows cross proofs remained **in progress**, and install proofs were **skipped** because gate failed.
- [CI run 38398392919](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38398392919) at `1aaabfa3` passed the Mac proof/carriers but exposed the FORCE_COLOR failure and missing install contexts repaired here. Windows cross separately failed with a store-journey `PermissionError`.
- At `c30c5dc`, [CI run 38757714990](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38757714990), read at approximately 2026-10-15T16:40Z, was **still in progress**. Mac and Windows cross proofs were **pending**; the manual diagnostic was **skipped**. Gate had **failed**, although `onepipeline-npm:test` passed with the lock-contention repair. Its single failure was `store::a_cache_enabled_github_store_reads_and_writes_like_an_uncached_store` at `tests/e2e/store.rs:4573` (request-cost equality), introduced on main in #884 and untouched by this diff. Isolated reruns timed out once and passed **2/3**; a follow-up was recorded. Install proofs were **skipped** after gate failed, and the protected Ubuntu/Windows install carriers correctly **failed**. Deny, msrv, smoke, release-compat, llmlint, pr-title, wheel, both wheel proofs, Ubuntu/Windows documented installs and `visual-docs / report (…)` **passed**. Engine currency failed identically on main. The retained record subsequently reports all required checks passing after reruns; that verdict predates the merges.
- At `810345e0`, [CI run 38859127652](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38859127652) was initially **in progress**, with its single [Mac PR proofs job](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38859127652/job/116837415206) **queued** and the manual diagnostic **skipped**. Gate, Windows cross, Windows documented install, llmlint, smoke, release-compat and both wheel proofs were running; changes, pr-title, deny, msrv and Ubuntu documented install had passed.
- For that same head, [engine currency](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38859127719/job/116837170110), [suppressions](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38859127831/job/116837170456) and [visual-docs preflight](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38859128297/job/116837172483) were initially pending. A later read found engine currency failed, suppressions and visual preflight passed, and visual capture running. [Release sweep](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38859127779/job/116837172043) was skipped for the ordinary PR.
- The completed `810345e0` CI run **failed gate** on one `onepipeline-npm:test` subtest: “refuses a ref rather than a commit as a base to judge against” (`npm/test/llmlint-cache.test.mjs:847`). Nx printed the command and non-zero exit but omitted the refusal emitted by `scripts/llmlint-judge.sh`; sibling refusals passed. The test, judge script and its Nx target are unchanged by this branch. Locally, the subtest passed **22/22** runs, including 20 concurrent runs and eight with CI environment variables. Lost output under Nx is the suspected cause, recorded as a follow-up rather than fixed here.
- The same run’s Mac proof failed `rework::a_restack_starts_before_its_reworked_parent_s_checks_have_settled`, introduced on main in #916 and untouched here; it failed **2/3** reruns. [Windows cross](https://github.com/nickderobertis/onepipeline/actions/runs/38859127652/job/116837415247) failed `driver::a_detached_adoption_whose_driver_dies_is_refused_with_what_that_driver_said`, which passed on rerun. Both have follow-ups. The install carriers failed because their prerequisites did.
- A local llmlint-cache suite run passed **59/60** tests; its teardown test failed because `spawnSync ps` exceeded its output buffer (`ENOBUFS`) on the shared host. That unchanged test also has a follow-up.

Observed gate duration was 68–73 minutes, with Windows cross taking 79–85 minutes on main. The final pending observation does not cover that critical path.

### Suppressions covered by this diff

Added or rewritten directives:

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:774,906` — `diagnostics_error_or_absent`: reproduce end-user installs without denying warnings; existing check jobs enforce compiler warnings.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml:601` — `SC2016`: interpolation belongs to Node at runtime.
- `.github/fixtures/visual-docs-reusable.yml:162` — `boundary_inputs_validated`: immutable upstream resolver fixture; the local interpreter validates its architecture inventory.
- `.github/workflow-schema.mjs:1` — `contracts_have_one_source_or_a_drift_gate`: allowlists define a closed interpreter subset; unsupported fields are refused and tested.
- `.github/workflow-schema.mjs:77` — `boundary_inputs_validated`: GitHub validates cron syntax; the interpreter validates mapping/string shape.
- `.github/telemetry.mjs:66` — `boundary_inputs_validated`: producer/reader journeys prove complete recording; deliberate row deletion is outside scope.
- `scripts/build-staged-release.py:306` — `work_goes_through_command_surface`: per-target staging composes the existing primitive in directories the fixed Nx output cannot express.
- `npm/test/artifact-transport.py:20` — `contracts_have_one_source_or_a_drift_gate`: the forge transport double models upload-artifact layout using actual workflow paths and real artifacts.

Standing directives covering changed lines:

- `.github/workflows/release.yml:130` — `no_second_broader_sweep_over_an_already_gated_commit`: a manually published tag may identify a commit CI never gated.
- `tests/nextest_runs.rs:1480` — `changed_behavior_has_e2e`: structural workflow assertions complement the real subprocess diagnostic journeys in that module; previously reported at line 1046.

Removed: the `contracts_have_one_source_or_a_drift_gate` directive on the former handwritten arm64 wheel check name, and the `SC2016` directive on the removed Rosetta wrapper.

body.body:
## What

Make stop wait for an in-flight write-back to save its landed baseline before ending the driver, so live-added tasks are released instead of stranded queued. Multi-source journeys wait out torn store reads while retaining their state assertions and rejecting other read failures.

Preserve every attached monitor event across re-renders, and include each failed node’s journal settlement detail when the readjust journey fails. Add regression coverage for the stop window, torn reads, and diagnostics.

## Why

The required Windows check passed only once in eight recent main runs, blocking the serde-saphyr change (#923) and review-feedback change (#935). Fixing the confirmed race and making the remaining failure diagnosable supports restoring reliable CI before further changes merge.

## Additional info

The readjust failure’s mechanism remains unidentified: it did not reproduce on this host. The monitor fix addresses lost diagnostic events, not a demonstrated cause of that journey’s failure.
